Senses.Explanation: In case collections and recorded sayings, an interjected comment (著語) is compact wording inserted against a cited exchange, often immediately after one of its lines and introduced by “appends a comment and says” (著語云). The Blue Cliff Record preserves Xuedou Chongxian's repeated comments such as “seen through,” and Yuanwu Keqin's recorded sayings insert “wrong” after successive turns of an older case. Wansong Xingxiu explicitly quotes comments by Yuanwu and then answers them from his own position. Tianyin Yuanxiu and Hongzhi Zhengjue likewise interrupt cited exchanges with short verdicts. A reviewed unnamed monastic questioner asks Langting Ting for a comment on a named case, while Xiangtian Jinian says he will place a comment against each line. The form can therefore name either the inserted wording or the act of adding it; it does not denote ordinary authorship where the verb authored merely precedes the noun recorded sayings.
